title: PLG→Sales signal definitions, thresholds, and success metrics (v1)
creator: Nikhil Sharma
project: PLG signals → HubSpot routing (Hosted → Dedicated/Private expansion)
related_prs: GitHub: sources/github/redwood/pr_9861.json (adds contact sales + pricing/security intent events; links PM-412)
description:
Goal
Finalize the v1 signal list (high-signal, low false positives), explicit thresholds, and success metrics for the PLG→sales-assisted expansion motion. Output should be concrete enough for ENG to implement scoring/dedupe and for Sales/CS/Ops to agree on what gets routed and how we measure whether it’s working.

Context
We are scaling from a self-serve Hosted API motion into measurable, sales-assisted expansion for Dedicated and Private. We will route “sales-worthy” usage and intent signals into HubSpot (timeline events + tasks + optional sequences) with suppression/cool-down. This ticket defines: (1) what counts as a signal, (2) thresholds by window, (3) success metrics + pilot gates.

Non-goals (v1)
- Building a full ML lead score model (rule-based only in v1).
- Deep firmographic enrichment (we’ll use domain/company name + lightweight enrichment when available; no requirement for coverage).
- Routing individual users (no user-level identifiers in the signal payload).

Definitions
- Account = HubSpot Company (mapped via workspace_id → company domain when known).
- “Net spend” = billed usage excluding promo/free credits.
- Windows: 7d / 14d / 30d rolling windows (refreshed daily; v1 SLA is daily refresh, with a stretch goal of 6-hour refresh for high-intent intent events).
- Cool-down = suppression period after a signal is emitted for a company (per signal type) to prevent repeated tasks/outreach.

V1 signal taxonomy (ship)
A) Usage growth / economics (expansion readiness)
1) Sustained spend growth (Hosted → Dedicated conversation)
- Trigger: (30d net spend >= $1,500) AND (7d net spend >= $500)
- Additional qualifier (one of):
  - 30d net spend growth >= 35% vs prior 30d, OR
  - 7d net spend growth >= 50% vs prior 7d
- Why it matters: indicates production usage with predictable baseline; Dedicated improves unit economics + throughput predictability.
- Cool-down: 14 days.
- Priority: High.

2) Throughput/concurrency pressure (Hosted → Dedicated conversation)
- Trigger (any one):
  - Peak concurrent inferences (max concurrent requests) >= 25 for >= 3 days in last 7 days, OR
  - Peak RPM >= 300 for >= 3 days in last 7 days, OR
  - Tokens/min (peak) >= 1.5M for >= 3 days in last 7 days
- Why it matters: sustained bursts lead to rate-limit friction and noisy latency; Dedicated provides predictable throughput with reserved capacity.
- Cool-down: 14 days.
- Priority: High.

B) Reliability / friction (pain-driven conversion)
3) Rate-limit pain (Quota friction)
- Trigger: 429/“rate_limited” responses >= 200 in 7d AND occurred on >= 3 distinct days in last 7d
- Secondary trigger (lower confidence, do not auto-enroll sequence): >= 50 in 7d AND (7d net spend >= $250)
- Why it matters: suggests they’re hitting self-serve guardrails; prompts Dedicated sizing or quota/burst policy conversation.
- Cool-down: 10 days.
- Priority: High.

4) Model routing / capacity errors (operational risk)
- Trigger: “model_routing_failed” OR “capacity_unavailable” errors >= 20 in 7d AND occurred on >= 3 distinct days
- Exclusion: if status page incident tagged as “platform-wide” overlaps >50% of those events, downgrade to “FYI” (HubSpot timeline only; no task).
- Why it matters: their workload is impacted; Dedicated capacity / multi-region fallback / configuration review may be needed.
- Cool-down: 10 days.
- Priority: Medium → High depending on spend (if 30d net spend >= $1,500 then High).

C) Explicit intent (buying motion)
5) “Contact sales” / demo request
- Trigger: contact_sales_event = true (from Console or marketing site)
- Why it matters: explicit inbound.
- Cool-down: 30 days (but allow manual re-open).
- Priority: Highest.

6) Security/compliance intent (Private/Dedicated enterprise readiness)
- Trigger (any one):
  - Viewed “SSO/SAML” docs >= 2 times in 14d OR
  - Viewed “Audit logs” docs >= 2 times in 14d OR
  - Viewed “SOC 2 / compliance” docs >= 2 times in 14d OR
  - Started “security questionnaire” flow event (single event qualifies)
- Qualification rule: if 30d net spend < $250 AND no explicit contact sales event, create HubSpot timeline event only (no task) to avoid noise.
- Why it matters: correlates with procurement/security review timelines; may indicate Private/VPC requirements.
- Cool-down: 21 days.
- Priority: High.

7) Data residency / region constraint intent
- Trigger: region_residency_intent event OR docs/console engagement with “EU-only”, “VPC”, “on-prem” pages >= 2 in 14d
- Qualification rule: if company geo = EMEA OR APAC OR selected region != us-east/us-west, raise priority.
- Cool-down: 21 days.
- Priority: Medium → High.

Signals explicitly NOT shipping in v1 (proposed v1.1)
- Repeated pricing page visits (marketing attribution is noisy; needs better identity stitching + bot filtering).
- “Time on page” engagement scoring.
- Advanced churn-risk signals (separate motion; avoid mixing with expansion).

Threshold calibration notes (from analysis v1)
- Target lead volume for pilot: ~15–30 tasks/week across pilot cohort (so AEs/SDRs can respond within SLA).
- False positives to avoid: early-stage hackers burning free credits; short-lived load tests; incident-driven spikes; internal/test domains.
- Spend thresholds use net spend to avoid free-credit distortions.

Routing requirements (inputs for PM-413)
- One HubSpot Company timeline event per signal emission + one task when “task-eligible”.
- Task-eligible signals in v1: Contact Sales, Sustained Spend Growth, Throughput/Concurrency Pressure, Rate-limit Pain (high confidence), Security Questionnaire Started.
- Timeline-only signals in v1: low-confidence security intent when spend < $250, region/residency intent without other qualifiers, model routing failures during platform-wide incidents.
- Required properties in event payload (no user PII): company_id/workspace_id, company domain (if known), signal_type, signal_version, window (7/14/30), metrics snapshot (aggregates only), first_seen_at, last_seen_at, recommended_next_step, links (console usage page, docs page category).

Dedupe + cool-down (inputs for ENG-2842)
- Idempotency key: company_id + signal_type + window_end_date (UTC) + signal_version.
- Cool-down is evaluated per company_id + signal_type; new emissions within cool-down should be suppressed unless severity increases (severity bump defined below).
- Severity bump override: if (30d net spend crosses >= $5,000) OR (429s increase >= 3x vs last emitted snapshot) then allow a new task despite cool-down, but mark as “escalation”.

Success metrics (pilot + ongoing)
Primary outcome metrics (weekly)
- Signal→Meeting: % of task-eligible signals that result in a meeting booked within 14 days.
- Signal→SQL: % of task-eligible signals that become SQL within 30 days.
- Signal→Pipeline: $ pipeline created within 45 days attributed to signal-triggered outreach.

Leading indicators / operational metrics (daily/weekly)
- Task creation SLA: p95 time from signal computed → HubSpot task created <= 2 hours (pilot) / <= 30 min (stretch).
- Delivery reliability: >= 99% HubSpot write success rate (excluding HubSpot outages) and automated retries/backoff.
- Dedupe quality: duplicate tasks from same signal_type per company <= 1% of task volume.
- Sales acceptance rate: >= 70% of tasks marked “relevant” by AE/SDR (simple disposition field), OR false positive rate <= 30%.
- Suppression correctness: 0 tasks created for “suppressed accounts” (enterprise/active opp/opt-out) in pilot.

Attribution rules (high-level; detailed in KPI spec)
- Attribute meeting/pipeline to a signal if:
  - The meeting is booked within 14 days of the first outreach attempt on the auto-created task, AND
  - Outreach was triggered by a HubSpot task created from a signal event (not purely inbound), AND
  - Company is not already in an active sales sequence/opportunity prior to the signal timestamp (suppression should prevent this, but we’ll also enforce in reporting).

Pilot gates (for PM-414)
- Week 1: Verify end-to-end correctness (events visible, tasks created, suppression working). Acceptable false positives <= 40% while we tune.
- Week 2: False positives <= 30% and p95 task creation <= 2h.
- Rollout gate to broader self-serve: false positives <= 20% and dedupe defects < 1% over 7 days.

Open questions (needs alignment)
1) Spend threshold by segment: do we want different spend bars for startup vs mid-market vs enterprise self-serve? Proposal: keep a single v1 bar; revisit post-pilot with volume data.
2) Concurrency definition: should we use max concurrent requests or “concurrent streaming responses”? Eng recommends max concurrent inferences at gateway since it’s stable; confirm with Telemetry.
3) “Security intent” without spend: should it create a task or timeline-only? Proposal above: timeline-only unless questionnaire started or explicit contact sales.
4) Ownership rules for EMEA residency intent: route to Lukas Meyer’s team by default when EMEA indicator present, even if billing country unknown?
5) Support-ticket coupling: if a support ticket exists for rate limits/latency, should that suppress SDR outreach and route to SE/CS instead?

Alignment checkpoints (required sign-offs)
- Sales leadership (Stephanie Nguyen / Lukas Meyer): confirm v1 signals are actionable; confirm acceptable lead volume & response-time expectation.
- CS (Jasmine Liu / Rachel Kim): confirm suppression rules for CSM-managed/enterprise accounts; confirm expansion handoff pattern.
- Security (Dr. Aisha Rahman / Marcus Lin): confirm payload fields and retention expectations; confirm no user PII.
- Biz Systems (David Kim / Isabelle Laurent): confirm required HubSpot objects/properties and workflow triggers.

Acceptance criteria
- v1 signals list + thresholds documented here and linked in PRD.
- Success metrics + pilot gates agreed in writing (Sales + CS + Security + Biz Systems).
- Any “timeline-only” vs “task-eligible” decisions explicitly captured.
- Open questions either resolved or explicitly deferred with an owner + date.

Decision log (current)
- 2025-02-04: Agreed v1 will prioritize usage + friction + explicit intent; marketing site engagement scoring deferred to v1.1.
- 2025-02-06: Security approved “no user identifiers”; company-level aggregates only.
- 2025-02-10: Sales leadership requested concrete thresholds and fewer “soft” intent signals; adopted spend + 429 + concurrency as core.
- 2025-03-07: Contact sales + security intent events added to telemetry stream (see PR 9861); v1 definitions considered locked for pilot.
comments: 2025-01-28 (Chris Osei): Pulled initial threshold candidates from historical cohorts; aiming for <=30 tasks/week in pilot. Drafted v1 taxonomy (spend, concurrency, 429s, security intent, residency intent).
2025-02-03 (Grace O'Connor): From SDR side: please avoid routing low-spend “security intent” unless it’s a questionnaire start or explicit contact sales; too many tire-kickers otherwise.
2025-02-05 (Nadia Rahman): Concurrency metric: gateway can reliably emit max concurrent requests; tokens/min is derived and can be delayed. Recommend using max concurrent + RPM for v1.

2025-02-06 (Dr. Aisha Rahman): Approved direction with constraints: no user emails/IDs; avoid URL-level page paths where they can leak sensitive context—use doc category enums instead. Add retention note in governance doc.
2025-02-10 (Stephanie Nguyen): Agree on spend + 429 + concurrency as the “spine”. Request: add an escalation rule for big spend jumps so we can re-engage even within cool-down.
2025-03-05 (David Kim): HubSpot needs clear delineation: which signals create tasks vs timeline-only. Also confirm idempotency key to prevent duplicate task storms during retries.
2025-03-07 (Nikhil Sharma): Marking PM-412 Done. v1 definitions locked for pilot. Any changes should go through change log + re-calibration review with Sales/CS weekly.
